prize_parts.citation: For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: I am moving from nanopore sensing (B003) to base editing (B011) with Liu alone, and I want to be explicit that this is a scientific judgment and not a count of hands. My round-1 test for B011 was whether it is a distinct chemical discovery or a CRISPR extension. Round 1 answered it better than I expected. The achievement is the programmed, site-specific chemical conversion of a nucleobase in a living cell, which is a new capability in kind: a change of one letter without cutting the DNA, rather than the cleavage and repair that the 2020 prize honoured. The adenine editor needed a deaminase that does not exist in nature, so directed evolution carried real chemical content, as Aqvist and Aili argued. Replication is extensive and first patients have been treated. Most important for a citation I have to explain to a broad audience, a Liu-only credit has a single originator and a simple sentence: the idea, the platform and the evolution programme come from one laboratory. It is the only leading candidate whose credit I can defend in one line. Two-name and three-name versions create the Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo disputes that no other leading candidate avoids.
statement.case_against: The 2020 prize is a real framing risk, and a single-laureate prize is narrow in a year with several mature multi-contributor fields. Komor and Gaudelli executed the founding papers, and Nishida and Kondo's Target-AID is an independent cytidine-deaminase design whose priority the citation wording must handle with care, for example by naming the programmed conversion of bases without double-strand cleavage and leaving the committee background text to record Target-AID. Off-target and bystander deamination are not fully characterised, as Chabes and Brzezinski note, and clinical benefit is early. I also accept that I am giving up what I still regard as the cleanest new measurement principle on the list, nanopore sensing, because I cannot resolve its five-way priority among Deamer, Branton, Kasianowicz, Bayley and Akeson into three names that I would defend publicly.

responses.point: Johan answered my round-1 question: the chemistry in base editing lies in the deaminase engineering and in programmed nucleobase modification, not in DNA cleavage, and Liu alone is the cleanest attribution.
responses.response: That is the argument I asked for and it moves me. Cleavage is what the 2020 prize honoured, whereas a one-base chemical conversion with directed evolution of the catalyst is a different act, and I now accept it as a distinct chemical discovery. I also accept Liu alone over the trio. I would still ask that the expert report quantify bystander and off-target deamination, which is where the physicist in me wants the evidence, but that is a point about the background text rather than a reason to defer.

responses.point: Peter asked what is new chemically in base editing beyond engineering of an existing CRISPR system, and said he would credit the adenine editor with its evolved deaminase if the committee goes this way.
responses.response: I shared that doubt in round 1 and it was my reason for ranking B003 first. I now think the evolved adenine deaminase, plus programmed cytidine deamination, answers it: the catalyst was invented, not borrowed. I also take your question about B058 seriously and I am not persuaded to move there; a C-N coupling prize would be a clean attribution but, as Peter Brzezinski says, an extension of 2010, and only you support it. I do not think the Crews-only B038 part you pair with it is defensible given Deshaies and Ciulli.

responses.point: Andrei argues that a prize recognises the discovery and its confirmed mechanism and not drug approval, so the missing approved degrader should not make B038 premature, and that the glue strand is a distinct discovery needing its own part.
responses.response: I concede the maturity point: I was too quick to call B038 early, since the ternary-complex mechanism is confirmed across many laboratories. My remaining objection is attribution. You say the glue strand needs a second part and that the three-person ceiling makes that costly, which is exactly why I cannot support a trio of Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli as the whole prize; the cereblon explanation of thalidomide would be written out. Both of us rank B011 second or third, and your own round-1 view that Liu alone is the cleanest configuration is where I now land. I keep B038 as an alternative.

responses.point: Xiaodong pairs nitrogenase (Rees, Einsle) with Liu-only base editing as a two-part prize and asks whether a structure-based achievement and an enabling method can gain a majority.
responses.response: I considered the pairing and I do not support it. Nitrogenase is a secure structure, and you and Peter Brzezinski both say the mechanism is open; a citation limited to the cofactor structure drops Dean, Seefeldt and Ribbe, whose kinetic and spectroscopic work cannot be separated from the structure. Combining that with B011 creates two parts, each with an attribution cost, and the three-person cap forces each to be thin. A single-part prize with one clear originator is easier to explain to the public than a compromise built to reach five votes. I would revisit the structure case in a year when the mechanism has firmed up.

responses.point: Daniel asks that the committee decide explicitly whether the base-editing trainees are named and not default to the principal investigator, and considers that the adenine editor depended on Gaudelli's directed evolution.
responses.response: That is a fair demand and I have decided. Prize logic rewards the originator of the idea and programme, and the founding papers carry Liu as the author of the platform; naming Komor and Gaudelli would also put Nishida and Kondo's priority on the table for the cytidine editor. I record the cost: the trainees are excluded by the three-person framing and by this judgment, not by any doubt about their experimental contribution.

uncertainties: Whether a Liu-only citation can hold up against the Komor and Gaudelli claims and the Nishida and Kondo Target-AID priority question once the expert report is read.
Whether the committee as a whole will see base editing as distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize; I am now persuaded, but a majority may not be.
How far off-target and bystander deamination, and the early state of clinical benefit, should count against maturity.
Whether any nanopore three-name split could be defended: I have not found one that omits neither Branton nor Kasianowicz, and I could be wrong that these claims cannot be separated from Deamer's.
statement.conflict_note: Updated from round 1: I have no personal or institutional tie to Liu or any other credited person for B011, B003 or B038, and I am no longer proposing B003, whose subject (nanopore sensing) is adjacent to my own nanowire and molecular-motor work. No recusal is requested.
